China's rare earth export controls threaten critical mineral supply chains 🇨🇦

Critical Minerals & Supply Chains
China's upcoming November export controls under Announcement No. 61 are widening the ex-China price gap for rare earths like dysprosium and terbium, accelerating the push toward independent regional supply chains. While higher global prices such as European dysprosium trading at nearly 5x domestic Chinese rates improve project economics, non-Chinese operators still face steep hurdles in securing processing equipment and technical expertise. Trade consultants and advisory practices should package specialized audits to help ex-China producers and recyclers audit their technology stacks, fast-track secondary feed processing, and de-risk supply chain dependencies before the November regulatory deadline.

Exploration & Capital Markets
Perseverance Metals' recent market surge highlights surging investor appetite for North American nickel, copper, and critical mineral assets alongside Voyageur Discovery's boosting impact. Despite successful initial drilling, bringing new critical mineral deposits to production in North America faces persistent delays and complex infrastructure gaps. Enterprise advisory firms can position technical services to help junior explorers accelerate resource delineation, optimize drilling campaigns, and de-risk early-stage metallurgical processing.

Global Infrastructure & Beneficiation
The Africa Finance Corporation is driving a push for local beneficiation and strategic infrastructure, including the $753 million Lobito Corridor showcased at African Mining Week 2026. This initiative addresses the value addition imperative of moving African economies beyond raw ore exports toward domestic processing, refining, and industrial manufacturing while unlocking landlocked mineral deposits via integrated rail networks connecting Central African production to Atlantic ports. Technical consulting practices should engage the Africa Finance Corporation and regional project developers to provide advisory on engineering, project finance structuring, and implementation frameworks for domestic processing facilities.

Regional Industrial Scaling
Saudi Arabia's mining and quarrying sector surged 19 percent in July 2026, boosting the Kingdom's industrial production index through accelerating capital deployment and operational scaling within the mineral sector. This expansion aligns with broader national efforts to elevate non-oil industrial activities and build a resilient, vertically integrated mining economy. Industrial stakeholders and regional operators should retain specialized advisory services focused on optimizing asset utilization, supply chain bottlenecks, and environmental performance during rapid production scaling.
